why:
Issue 2762 -- the bound on re-entrant log sinks: how many deliveries to sinks that declared `LogSink::reentrant()` may be in progress at once before a record takes the guarded, one-at-a-time path instead. It stops a re-entrant sink that logs from inside its own `log()` from recursing without bound, and it is public so a test (and a sink author) can reason about that bound.

rclrs has no correspondent: its logging is `rclrs::log!` over rcutils, whose output handler is a single process-wide callback that rcutils serialises with its own lock, so the question of which sinks may run concurrently never arises there.
